'simulate_scene' has 2 input-scaling loops nested together — O(n^2).
Why it matters: The sizes come in as parameters, so if both can grow this is genuinely quadratic.
What to do: Replace an equality inner-lookup with a set/dict, or confirm the inputs stay small.
Why flagged: 2 nested loops that both scale with (unknown) input sizes.
Impact (measured, no LLM): O(n^2) → O(n)
  How long ONE lookup takes as the collection grows (N = number of items in it):
    list ▁▂▂▃▃▄▄▅▅▆▆▇▇██  a list is scanned item-by-item, so it gets slower the bigger it is (up to ~38.7 µs)
    set  ▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁  a set/dict jumps straight to the answer, so it stays the same at any size (~7 ns)
  ⚠ HOW BIG IS THIS COLLECTION? We cannot tell — it is not a literal here, so its
     size is whatever the caller passes at run time. That makes the cost
     CONDITIONAL, and the two cases are far apart: a small fixed list (a handful
     of names) wastes almost nothing, while a collection that grows with your
     input gets slower worse than proportionally — twice the data is about four
     times the time. Find your own N on the chart above to read your case.
  The GROWING case drawn to scale, if the loop also runs about once per item
  (an illustration — we did not measure your real N):
  ~774.3 ms ┤                                       •••  list (with a list)
            │                                   ••••   
            │                              •••••       
            │                        ••••••            
            │              ••••••••••                  
          0 │••••••••••••••····························  set (stays almost flat)
            └──────────────────────────────────────────
             N=0                                 20,000
  So IF N reaches 20,000, one full pass would waste about ~774.3 ms on pure searching, versus about ~147.0 µs with a set — roughly 5267x less. If N is small and fixed, this line does not apply to you.
